- Any logs or traces you can share that show per-tenant KV cache boundaries and eviction events (sanitized) would be helpful.

Quick update — I attached a diagram (kvcache-segmentation-diagram.png) showing how per-tenant KV namespaces are scoped inside the inference process: namespace ID is derived from tenant ID, each namespace maps to a separate KV shard allocated from host memory/GPU memory and tracked by the runtime allocator. Key points:

- Dedicated deployment: customers can be pinned to GPU pools comprised of whole GPUs (no hardware level multiplexing by default).
- For shared-host cases (rare, for burst/spot scenarios) we enforce cgroup + MIG partitioning where supported and runtime-level namespace isolation.
- KV cache entries are tagged with tenant namespace and include TTL + LRU eviction per-namespace. Global OOM triggers run a tenant-aware eviction policy (low-priority tenants evicted first in mixed pools).

I'll also attach the sanitized eviction log and a snippet of the runtime config that shows tenant_pin: true and per-tenant qos settings.

Adding the runtime perspective — summary for the SIG response we should send to Acme:

1) Physical tenancy model:
- Dedicated: Entire GPU devices are reserved to the customer's pool (VM/instance/GPU allocation) when Dedicated is selected. No scheduler-level multiplexing across tenant workloads on the same GPU device for Dedicated reservations.
- Shared/burst: when customers opt into shared capacity, we use strict cgroups, optional MIG and tenant-aware runtime slicing.

2) KV cache separation:
- Namespacing by tenant ID, enforced at runtime allocator level. Keys include tenant prefix; allocator rejects cross-namespace fetches.
- Per-namespace LRU + TTL; eviction is tenant-scoped. Global pressure triggers tenant-priority policy.

3) Noisy neighbor mitigations:
- GPU-level: MIG (NVIDIA) optional partitions, device-level isolation on Dedicated, per-tenant scheduling weights on shared pools.
- System-level: NIC QoS, bandwidth shaping, NUMA-aware placement to avoid PCIe contention.
- Runtime-level: token-rate throttling, preemption-friendly batch windowing, and proactive cache warming for high-SLA tenants.

4) Observability / evidence:
- Tenant-scoped eviction logs, tenant-labeled traces, per-tenant telemetry dashboards.
- We will provide sanitized samples and the runbook section that explains how we prove tenant boundaries during audits.

Neha
Neha Kapoor

Alice — attaching the requested items for your SIG review. Short executive summary below; full details are attached.

Executive summary:
- Dedicated mode: customers are assigned reserved GPU devices for their Dedicated pools. We do not multiplex multiple Dedicated tenants onto the same physical GPU device.
- KV cache: per-tenant namespace tagging enforced at the runtime allocator level. Keys are tenant-prefixed; allocator and API layer prevent cross-tenant access. Per-namespace LRU + TTL; global pressure triggers tenant-priority eviction (configurable).
- Noisy-neighbor controls: optional MIG partitions, cgroup isolation on shared hosts, NIC QoS and NUMA-aware placement to limit PCIe contention. Runtime-level throttles and preemption policies protect tail-latency SLAs.
- Evidence: sanitized eviction logs, kvcache segmentation diagram, runtime config snippet (tenant_pin, qos weights) attached. We also included links to the runbook that explains audit steps.

Attachments: SIG-questionnaire-filled.pdf, kvcache-segmentation-diagram.png, dedicated-runtime-config.yaml
